title: Guideline: sodium intake for adults and children
key_support: WHO recommends reducing sodium intake; in adults, reduction to <2 g/day sodium is recommended to reduce blood pressure and cardiovascular risk.
limitations: Population-level guidance; selected clinical conditions may require physician-supervised diets.

title: Effect of dose and duration of reduction in dietary sodium on blood pressure levels
key_support: 133 randomized trials (12,197 participants); sodium reduction lowered SBP/DBP and showed a dose-response relationship.
limitations: Effect magnitude varies by baseline blood pressure, age and population; short trials can underestimate effects.

title: Guideline: potassium intake for adults and children
key_support: WHO provides evidence-informed recommendations to increase potassium intake to reduce noncommunicable disease risk, including blood-pressure-related risk.
limitations: Population-level guidance; food intake and supplementation should not be assumed equivalent for all populations.

organization: Journal of the American Heart Association
title: Potassium Intake and Blood Pressure: A Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
key_support: 32 trials identified a nonlinear relationship; BP-lowering effects were stronger in hypertension and at higher sodium intake.
limitations: High potassium supplementation estimates were less certain; excessive supplementation should not be inferred as beneficial.

title: Carbohydrate intake for adults and children: WHO guideline
key_support: WHO emphasizes carbohydrate quality and recommends adults consume at least 25 g/day of naturally occurring dietary fibre.
limitations: Daily dietary recommendation; cannot be directly applied to a dish record until serving/basis semantics are resolved.

title: Carbohydrate quality and human health: a series of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
population: general population without chronic disease in included prospective studies/trials
key_support: Higher fibre intake was associated with lower all-cause/CVD mortality, CHD, stroke, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer; trials improved weight, SBP and total cholesterol.
limitations: Long-term disease estimates rely substantially on observational cohorts; applicability was population-level rather than chronic-disease treatment.

title: Saturated fatty acid and trans-fatty acid intake for adults and children: WHO guideline
population: adults and children aged 2+ for main intake guidance
key_support: WHO recommends no more than 10% of total energy from saturated fat and emphasizes replacement with unsaturated fats or carbohydrate from naturally fibre-rich foods.
limitations: Requires total energy and replacement context; dish-level grams alone cannot establish guideline compliance.

title: Reduction in saturated fat intake for cardiovascular disease
population: adults with or without cardiovascular disease; long-term trials
key_support: 15 RCTs (56,675 participants); reducing saturated fat for at least 2 years reduced combined cardiovascular events by about 17%.
limitations: Little/no clear effect on all-cause or cardiovascular mortality; individual endpoint evidence was less certain and replacement context matters.
